dcf.method: 5-year FCFF: EBITDA - tax on EBIT - capex - change in net working capital; growth fades linearly from the starting rate to the year-5 rate; Gordon terminal value; equity = EV - borrowings.

reverse_dcf.note: Constant sales growth for five years, at the base margin and the same WACC and terminal growth, that makes the DCF equal today's EV.

blocks.text: [F] Axtel Industries Ltd designs and manufactures custom process-engineering equipment and complete process plants for the food industry, covering everything from receiving raw material through to the final processing stages (RATING) (AR2026 p.55). [F] It reports a single segment, 'Machinery and Equipment' (AR2026 p.93). [F] In FY26, revenue from operations was Rs 223.77 cr. Of this, Rs 215.42 cr (96.3%) came from machines manufactured, Rs 7.21 cr (3.2%) from installation, commissioning and other services, and Rs 1.14 cr (0.5%) from scrap (AR2026 p.81). [F] Revenue from machines is recognised at a point in time, on dispatch, delivery or customer acceptance; service revenue is recognised over time (AR2026 p.72).

[F] CARE lists the end markets as confectionery, malted drinks, aqua feed, ready-to-eat foods, bakery and biscuits, dairy, beverages, instant mixes, snack foods, spices, and condiments and seasoning (RATING). [F] The company does not disclose a revenue split by end market or product family. **The end-market percentage split asked for in this report cannot be built from the disclosures** (AR2026 p.55, p.93). [F] By geography, FY26 revenue was Rs 196.88 cr domestic (88.0%) and Rs 26.89 cr exports (12.0%), compared with 83.7% / 16.3% in FY25 (AR2026 p.93). [MC] The customer base is described as Indian and multinational food companies, including Nestle, Cadbury, ITC, Unilever, Mondelez, Barry Callebaut and Haldiram's (AR2026 p.12). [F] CARE puts the customer count at more than 150 (RATING).

[F] Axtel is not a recent listing. It was incorporated in 1991 as Advanced Extrafoil Technology and Exports Limited, started commercial production in 1993, and is listed on BSE under scrip code 523850 (RATING) (AR2026 p.1, p.11). [F] The company makes no presentations to institutional investors or analysts (AR2026 p.49). [AI] No earnings-call transcripts, investor presentations or prospectus were available. The evidence base is therefore the FY26 annual report, a February 2026 CARE rating note, exchange announcements and screener.in data. That is thin for a company of this size and it widens the error bars on every forward view.

subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. Valuation requires growth the company has never delivered. [F] The reverse DCF implies a 34.5% five-year sales CAGR, against 8.8% in the base case (NUMBERS). [F] Actual sales CAGRs are 7.6% over 3 years, 7.9% over 5 years and 12.8% over 9 years (NUMBERS). [F] The bull-case value of Rs 251.5 is 43.9% below the Rs 448 price (NUMBERS).

2. Revenue is lumpy and cyclical. [F] Sales fell from Rs 223 cr in FY24 to Rs 179 cr in FY25 before recovering to Rs 224 cr in FY26 (NUMBERS). [F] CARE cites dependence on end-user capex cycles and fixed-price contracts (RATING). [E] FY26 sales were essentially flat on FY24, so the 'growth' is a cycle recovery.
3. Q1 FY27 margin collapsed. [F] Jun-26 quarter EBITDA margin was 7.83% on sales of Rs 32.31 cr, against 21.5% in the Mar-26 quarter (NUMBERS).

4. Large unexplained cost line. [F] 'Other selling expenses' rose from Rs 0.76 cr to Rs 13.92 cr (6.2% of revenue) with no explanation in the annual report (AR2026 p.82). Over the same period material cost fell 6.8pp of revenue (AR2026 p.81-82). [AI] The margin story cannot be audited from outside without an explanation of this line.

5. Promoter remuneration is rising fast relative to profit. [F] Each whole-time director's pay rose 33.33% in FY26 to Rs 2.40 cr, while non-managerial salaries rose an average of 0.63% (AR2026 p.33). [F] The ceiling is being raised to Rs 3.60 cr each from 1 Aug 2026 (AR2026 p.5, p.11). [E] Together that is up to Rs 7.2 cr, or 23% of FY26 PAT.

6. Key-person and succession risk. [F] The two founder-executives are 67 and 69 (AR2026 p.12, p.15). [F] 'Technology developed by the Whole-time Directors' and R&D expenditure is 'N.A.' (AR2026 p.31). [AI] No successor is identified.

7. Thin disclosure and inconsistent reporting. [F] There is no order book, customer concentration, capacity or product mix in the annual report. Director remuneration is shown as Rs 360 lakh in note 22 but Rs 480 lakh in the related-party note (AR2026 p.82, p.92). The current ratio is shown as 2.09 in the MD&A and 1.14 in the ratio note (AR2026 p.56, p.93).

8. Exports are shrinking. [F] Export revenue fell 7.5% to Rs 26.89 cr in FY26 and its share fell from 16.3% to 12.0% (AR2026 p.93). [F] Actual foreign-exchange earned fell to Rs 23.60 cr from Rs 29.78 cr (AR2026 p.31).

9. Related-party advisory fee paid to the brother of an executive director, who sits on the audit and nomination and remuneration committees. [F] Morphis Business Advisory LLP received Rs 48 lakh in FY26; Ameet Nalin Parikh is a partner (AR2026 p.32, p.92). [F] The governance report nonetheless states there was no pecuniary relationship with non-executive directors beyond sitting fees (AR2026 p.48).
10. Single plant. [F] Everything is made at one facility, at Halol, Gujarat (RATING) (AR2026 p.50).

Is FY26 margin structural? Bull view: [F] the FY26 EBITDA margin of 18% matched FY24's 20% range (NUMBERS). Bear view: [F] Q1 FY27 was 7.83% and FY25 was 13% (NUMBERS); [F] CARE describes margins as volatile and mix-dependent (RATING). [AI] Over FY17-FY26 EBITDA margin has ranged from 12% to 20% with no upward trend.

Is cash generation better than profit? Bull view: [F] 3-year CFO/PAT is 1.74x (NUMBERS). Bear view: [F] the audited FY26 CFO of Rs 51.06 cr is Rs 20 cr below our statements data's Rs 71 cr (AR2026 p.68) (NUMBERS); [AI] much of FY26 CFO came from a Rs 25.0 cr rise in payables and other liabilities, including customer advances, which reverses when order intake slows (AR2026 p.68).

Does the order book underwrite growth? Bull view: [F] about Rs 250 cr at Sep-25 (RATING). Bear view: [F] the same CARE note also says 'over Rs 200 crore' (RATING); [F] the company itself discloses no order book (AR2026 p.55-56); [E] about Rs 161 cr of revenue has been booked since Sep-25 (H2 FY26 plus Q1 FY27) (NUMBERS).

Is the treasury book an underappreciated asset? [F] Rs 97.7 cr of cash and mutual funds sits outside the EV in our valuation data (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.66). [AI] Adding the treasury to the bull-case equity value of Rs 406.4 cr still leaves it well short of the Rs 724 cr market cap (NUMBERS).

Is the shareholder register a liquidity or governance risk? [F] Promoters own 49.95%, unchanged for 12 quarters, about 38% of it through two LLPs (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.79). [F] 10.71% of shares are still held in physical form (AR2026 p.50).

blocks.text: [AI] Our view differs from the market's mainly on valuation, not on business quality. Axtel looks like a well-run, cash-generative, debt-free niche engineer-to-order shop with a credit rating upgraded to CARE A- in Feb-25 (RATING). But it is cyclical, with revenue of Rs 223 cr in FY24, Rs 179 cr in FY25 and Rs 224 cr in FY26 (NUMBERS). At Rs 448 the price already discounts a growth path roughly four times the company's own history: a 34.5% implied CAGR against a 7.6-12.8% record (NUMBERS). [AI] On disclosed evidence, the overlooked point is not upside. It is that peak-cycle FY26 margins, a Rs 13.92 cr unexplained cost line and a sharp step-up in promoter pay leave little room for disappointment. The best counter-argument is that the stock is a thinly traded asset-light compounder whose treasury and dividend support a floor that DCF-on-sales understates.

blocks.text: [AI] This is a mature business, about 33 years in operation, run by the same two founders, whose know-how traces back to 1985. That is the opposite of a recently built business. The record is long enough to show the cycle: [F] revenue reached Rs 111 cr in FY19, dipped to Rs 100 cr in FY20, hit Rs 153 cr in FY21, fell to Rs 144 cr in FY22, then went to Rs 223 cr in FY24, Rs 179 cr in FY25 and Rs 224 cr in FY26 (NUMBERS). The recent events are mostly governance and capital-allocation items (rating upgrade, investment limits, ESOP, pay increases), plus a first external technology licence in Sep-26. None of them is a new business line.

items: 1. Enquiry and process design. [MC] Each plant is custom-designed to the client's requirement; design and engineering is run by Ajay N. Parikh (AR2026 p.13, p.55).

2. Order and advance. [F] Customers pay advances: Rs 33.94 cr was outstanding at Mar-26 (AR2026 p.80). [F] Performance bank guarantees were Rs 12.96 cr (AR2026 p.83). [MC] Most raw material is bought when the order is received (RATING).

3. Procurement. [F] FY26 material consumption was Rs 91.94 cr, of which SS/MS steel was only Rs 11.24 cr and 'others', mainly bought-out components, were Rs 80.70 cr (AR2026 p.81). [F] Imported material was Rs 0.47 cr (0.5%) (AR2026 p.83).

4. Fabrication and assembly at Halol. [F] One plant; Rs 13.54 cr spent on labour and job-work charges, an outsourcing indicator (AR2026 p.82). [F] CARE notes 'strategic partnership for other specialised operations' (RATING).
5. Dispatch and revenue recognition. [F] Revenue is recognised on dispatch, delivery or customer acceptance (AR2026 p.72).
6. Erection, commissioning and service. [F] Erection and commissioning cost Rs 5.60 cr; service revenue was Rs 7.21 cr (AR2026 p.81-82).

blocks.text: [AI] Value sits in process design and system integration, not in metal-working. [F] In FY26 the company spent Rs 94.84 cr on materials, including the change in WIP, against revenue of Rs 223.77 cr (AR2026 p.81-82). [E] Material-only gross margin was about 57.6%, up from 50.8% in FY25. [F] Employee cost of Rs 43.06 cr (19.2% of revenue) is the second-largest cost, which fits an engineering-hours business (AR2026 p.82). [MC] CARE ties margin to 'complexity and level of customisation' (RATING).

[F] Net fixed assets were Rs 31 cr against sales of Rs 224 cr in FY26, a fixed-asset turnover of 7.23x (NUMBERS). [F] Capex has run at 1.3%-4.9% of sales over ten years (NUMBERS). [F] There are no material leases and no capital commitments (AR2026 p.74, p.91). [AI] The business is asset-light; its binding constraint is engineering talent and promoter bandwidth, not plant.

[F] The annual report gives no product-wise revenue, margins or volumes; it describes a single segment of 'food processing instruments/equipments' (AR2026 p.55). The table below is built from CARE's application list and the revenue-type note. Growth and margin columns are our judgement.

subsections.title: 1. Domestic FMCG and food-processing plants (88% of revenue)

blocks.text: [F] Domestic revenue was Rs 196.88 cr in FY26 (AR2026 p.93). [AI] Axtel sits at the plant-design and equipment-supply stage of the value chain. It does not do civil works or packaging lines, and these are not mentioned. [F] There is no government or public-sector exposure in the documents. Customers are private FMCG and food companies (RATING) (AR2026 p.12). [AI] What exists today is a revenue base of roughly Rs 180-225 cr a year, swinging with client capex. What is narrative: the MD&A's multinational supply-chain diversification theme (AR2026 p.55).

[F] On 7 Sep 2026 Axtel signed an exclusive technology licence with IISc's FSID for a cryogenic grinding system. Consideration is up to Rs 3 cr plus royalties (ANNOUNCEMENTS). [F] This is the company's first disclosed external technology; the FY26 annual report records no imported technology and no R&D spend (AR2026 p.31). [AI] Strategically it signals a move to widen the product range beyond in-house founder-designed equipment. No revenue, pricing, launch date or customer is disclosed, and royalty terms are not public. We assign no value.

blocks.text: [F] Capacity and utilisation are not disclosed in any document. [MC] Management says it 'has expanded its production capacity by expansion of its existing factory shed and installed more machineries to cope with the rise in orders' (AR2026 p.12). [F] FY26 additions included land of Rs 2.41 cr, factory building Rs 0.82 cr, plant and machinery Rs 2.31 cr and office building Rs 0.81 cr (AR2026 p.75). The purpose of the land purchase is not stated. [AI] The 62% rise in labour and job-work charges, against a 25% rise in revenue, suggests peak FY26 demand was met partly through outsourcing rather than in-house capacity.

[E] The best demonstrated quarterly revenue is Rs 70.57 cr (Q4 FY26). Annualised, that is about Rs 282 cr, or 23% above TTM sales of Rs 229 cr (NUMBERS). This is a sensitivity that shows the current set-up can, at peak, support roughly that level. It is not a forecast. [F] Fixed-asset turnover was 7.23x in FY26 against a 13.85x peak in FY23 (NUMBERS). [AI] On FY23's turnover, today's Rs 31 cr fixed-asset base would be far from binding.
[F] There are 'no identifiable material leases' (AR2026 p.74), and the land is freehold (AR2026 p.70). No lease expiries exist to track.

blocks.caption: Capex history (Rs cr; capex from our statements data)

blocks.text: [F] Capex and ratios are from our statements data (NUMBERS). [F] The audited cash-flow statement shows FY26 PPE purchases of Rs 7.86 cr and FY25 of Rs 6.98 cr (AR2026 p.68). CWIP was Rs 0.35 cr at Mar-26 (AR2026 p.66). Our statements data shows nil, which is a rounding difference (NUMBERS).

[E] From FY21 to FY26, sales rose Rs 71 cr (Rs 153 cr to Rs 224 cr) on cumulative capex of Rs 33 cr (FY22-FY26), or about Rs 2.2 of incremental sales per rupee of capex (NUMBERS). [E] Net fixed assets almost doubled, from Rs 16 cr to Rs 31 cr, while sales grew 46%, so fixed-asset turnover fell from 9.56x to 7.23x (NUMBERS). [AI] Recent capex has gone into buildings, land, vehicles (Rs 2.44 cr in FY25) and solar rather than directly into output-linked machinery (AR2026 p.31, p.75).

[F] No capex plan, budget or funding plan is disclosed; capital commitments are nil (AR2026 p.91). [F] Prior-year CWIP of Rs 0.84 cr was capitalised with nil interest capitalisation, and all remaining CWIP is under one year old (AR2026 p.84). [AI] The business is clearly asset-light.
